objectives: Hear and identify /n/ in initial and final positions.
Distinguish /n/ from previously taught consonants, especially /m/.
Connect the /n/ phoneme to the lowercase n grapheme.
concepts: /n/ is a consonant phoneme that can occur at the beginning or end of simple words.
Accurate phoneme identification requires attentive listening before looking for a grapheme.
Minimal contrasts help distinguish /n/ from similar taught sounds such as /m/.

definitions.definition: The smallest sound unit that can distinguish words.
A written letter or letter group used to represent a sound.
The first phoneme heard in a word.
The last phoneme heard in a word.

workedExamples: nap begins /n/ → connect the first sound to n.
man ends /n/ → listen to the final sound before identifying n.
nap and map begin with different sounds: /n/ versus /m/.
commonMistakes: Looking at the word before listening.
Identifying the letter but not the sound.
revisionPoints: Hear /n/ → locate position → connect /n/ to n.

application: Locate /n/ at the beginning or end of simple words.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why listening is needed before selecting a grapheme.
mixedReview: Review m/s/t/p and add n discrimination.

mistakeBasedRevision: If /n/ and /m/ are confused, compare nap/map and say the first sound slowly.
weakTopicRevision: Repeat initial /n/ discrimination, then final /n/ discrimination.

activities.name: Sound hunt
steps: State whether /n/ is first or last.

outcomes: Learner identifies initial /n/ with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner identifies final /n/ with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner distinguishes /n/ from /m/ in simple contrasts with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner connects /n/ to the grapheme n with at least 90% accuracy.
